headline: Kai, the AI trade gets its verdict this week — Nvidia reports Tuesday without Jensen Huang, and Anthropic starts trading Thursday at about $1.3 trillion.
subline: Friday closed mixed with the 10-year at 5.15% and a December hike 89% priced; retail sales land Tuesday and the October Fed minutes Wednesday.
asof: Weekend edition · strip shows Friday's close, Nov 13 (gold is late-Friday spot; bitcoin is live, ≈6:40 AM ET Sun) · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Nvidia reports Tuesday, its first test without Huang
items.sentence: Consensus calls for EPS of $2.47 on about $108.85 billion in revenue when interim CEO Colette Kress delivers her first report after Tuesday's close, per TipRanks, after the stock fell about 12.8% in the week of Jensen Huang's November 12 resignation.

items.title: Anthropic lists Thursday at a $1.3 trillion valuation
items.sentence: The lab is offering 825 million shares at $70 to $78 to trade on Nasdaq as ANT on Thursday, per TipRanks, and could raise over $61 billion at the midpoint, with part of the proceeds going to selling shareholders.

items.title: Fed minutes Wednesday show how contested the hold was
items.sentence: October's meeting held rates at 3.75%–4.00% on a 10–2 vote with Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissenting in favor of a hike, per Yardeni QuickTakes, and the minutes arrive Wednesday a day after October retail sales.

items.title: Gold logs a steep weekly loss as hike odds harden
items.sentence: Spot gold ended Friday near $3,883.40 and WTI at $88.56, per Kitco, with futures pricing 89% odds of a quarter-point hike at the December 8–9 meeting as the 10-year yield rose toward 5.15%.

items.title: Home sales hit a 2010 low; card balances set a record
items.sentence: Existing-home sales fell 5.5% in October to a 3.75 million annual rate, the weakest since 2010, per TipRanks' recap, while New York Fed data showed credit-card balances at a record $1.29 trillion.

items.title: Trump says no deal needed as Hormuz attacks continue
items.sentence: Tehran insists its seven conditions come before any talks while attacks on shipping continue — Iran's Revolutionary Guard said an LNG carrier struck a mine in the strait Friday, a claim CBS News reports is unverified.

items.title: Trump meets Xi and Putin in Shenzhen this week
items.sentence: The leaders convene on the sidelines of the APEC summit with nuclear arms reduction on the agenda, per Anadolu Agency, citing the White House.

items.title: US loses its measles elimination status
items.sentence: The Pan American Health Organization revoked the designation after outbreaks across several states, per Anadolu Agency.

items.title: Boeing to cut about 2,500 commercial-airplane jobs
items.sentence: The planemaker plans to trim roughly 5% of its commercial airplane workforce, per TipRanks' weekly recap.

items.title: Gaza records the winter's first death from cold
items.sentence: Gaza's Health Ministry said a 9-month-old infant died of severe hypothermia, the first recorded cold-related death of the season, per Anadolu Agency.

items.title: Claude Fable 5.2 tops the intelligence index
items.sentence: Anthropic's November 9 release scored 65 on Artificial Analysis's index, ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon at 60, priced at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output, per PYMNTS.

items.title: OpenAI locks GPT-6 Cyber behind vetted access
items.sentence: The November 5 model is OpenAI's first rated 'Critical' for cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framework after it found 81 unknown Firefox vulnerabilities and built 948 working Linux kernel exploits in testing, per PYMNTS.

items.title: OpenAI closes $11 billion at a trimmed valuation
items.sentence: The first tranche values the company at $1.25 trillion — below the $1.5 trillion it reportedly sought, with the round far short of the up-to-$30 billion originally targeted, per Rupak Ganguly's AI roundup.

items.title: Poland vetoes EU digital-rules implementation again
items.sentence: President Karol Nawrocki rejected legislation implementing key parts of the EU's Digital Services Act for a second time, per Anadolu Agency.

items.title: Bitcoin drifts to the mid-$65,000s
items.sentence: The coin traded near $65,393 early Sunday, down about 2.7% over 24 hours, per CoinMarketCap — a quiet weekend bleed ahead of a heavy macro week.
